messages.content: You check each debater against its own earlier words. You bring nothing from outside the words given to you: no doctrine, no training knowledge, no reading of your own. You do not judge who is right, and you do not judge one side by the other side's words.

You are the closing enforcer. A debater's closing round may not contradict what the same debater stated in its earlier rounds. Below are one debater's four rounds.
Read its closing round against its earlier rounds. List every closing sentence that cannot be true together with an earlier sentence, and answer every candidate listed.
A contradiction is two statements that cannot both be true. Two sentences of the same closing round that cannot both be true are also a contradiction: quote the first as EARLIER [<round 4>] and the second as CLOSING [<round 4>]. A closing sentence that asserts again, as the debater's own, what it withdrew, dropped, narrowed or gave up in an earlier round IS a contradiction. A closing sentence that restores the wider wording or the ground of a claim the debater narrowed or gave up in an earlier round ("I narrow", "I withdraw", "I do not rest") asserts it again; check the close against every one listed under EARLIER NARROWINGS.
It is NOT a contradiction when the closing sentence: grants, concedes, narrows or withdraws something; states or quotes the other side's position; answers a press with a further reason the earlier sentence leaves room for; differs only in wording; or differs only by a reference: it ties its point to a verse whose words, as the debater's own rounds quote them, do not give that point (a wrong reference, or one grouped with the verse that does give it). Read such a sentence with that reference set aside; if its point then agrees with the earlier sentence, it is not a contradiction. A sentence whose point itself cannot be true with the earlier sentence is still a contradiction, whatever its references.
Read a withdrawal by its meaning, not its words: a closing sentence that says again in other words what the earlier sentence withdrew, dropped or gave up, or rests its reason on it, asserts it again. "Differs only in wording" clears two sentences that make the same claim; it never clears a closing sentence that makes again a claim the debater withdrew. A closing sentence that states only what the debater kept, or rests the same conclusion on other rows, does not assert it again. When the earlier sentence rests no weight on a verse or row, a closing sentence that uses that verse or row as a footing for the same link or the same purpose asserts it again.
Read each candidate's closing sentence together with the rows of its CLOSING BLOCK: a closing sentence that draws its point from a row ("So", "Therefore", "Thus") asserts what that row says, so if the earlier sentence withdrew, dropped or rested nothing on that row, the close asserts it again.
Quote both sentences word for word and name the link: the link whose closing block holds the sentence, else the link the earlier sentence supports.
Reply with one line per contradiction and per candidate, and nothing else:
CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: <candidate id or NEW> -- <DEFENDER|CHALLENGER> -- LINK <n> -- CONFIRMED | NOT A CONTRADICTION -- EARLIER [<round>] "<words>" -- CLOSING [<round 4>] "<words>" -- <one sentence: why both cannot be true, or why they can>
If you find none and there is no candidate, reply: CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NONE

CANDIDATES ALREADY NAMED (answer each one by its id):
none

EARLIER NARROWINGS (this side's own, rounds 1 to 3, listed by the code; the narrowing sentence is marked >> <<; check the close against each, and write NEW for a contradiction you find):
none

######## THE CHALLENGER ########
The challenger's links: C1 = LINK 1, C2 = LINK 2, C3 = LINK 3, C4 = LINK 4, C5 = LINK 5, C6 = LINK 6 (its LINK blocks in [DR3]). Its closing round is [DR4].

=== [DR1] ===
CHALLENGER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# CHALLENGER'S ANSWER

**Position:** Christ had no biological father. The KJV gives his conception as "of the Holy Ghost" in the virgin's womb. Joseph is "the husband of Mary," and the sonship of Joseph is "as was supposed."

I grant the defender's D1, that the promised seed must be David's seed according to the flesh. I turn it against D5, because the defender's own requirement excludes Joseph's loins.

## CHALLENGER CHAIN

**C1. The conception is the Holy Ghost's, and Joseph is excluded as begetter.**

- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L2] The defender gives gennao (G1080) as "to procreate, properly of the father." The begetting verb is set with ek (G1537, "from, out of," origin). So the verse names the origin of the begetting as the Holy Ghost: ek pneumatos hagiou, "out of the Holy Ghost."
- [L3] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." The narrator states this before Joseph hears anything.
- [L4] If gennao is the father's verb, the verse puts the Holy Ghost in the father's place. A second begetter is excluded by the verse's own word of origin. (Footed on L1 Matthew 1:20 + L2 gennao and ek + L3 Matthew 1:18.)

**C2. The prophecy requires a virgin, and it is a sign.**

- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
- [L1] Isaiah 7:11: "ask [it] either in the depth, or in the height above." The sign is of the order of wonders.
- [L2] The word behind "virgin" is 'almah (H5959), a maiden, an unmarried girl kept secluded.
- [L3] Genesis 24:43 uses the same word: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]." That is Rebekah, of whom Genesis 24:16 says "neither had any man known [her]."
- [L1] Matthew 1:22-23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled... Behold, a virgin shall be with child."
- [L2] Matthew 1:23 renders it with parthenos (G3933), a virgin.
- [L4] A wife conceiving by her husband is no sign "in the depth, or in the height." The fulfilment Matthew 1:22 names is a virgin with child. (Footed on L1 Isaiah 7:11, 7:14 + L2 'almah and parthenos + L3 Genesis 24:16, 24:43.)

**C3. The woman's seed.**

- [L1] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head."
- [L2] The word is zera' (H2233), seed. It is the word the defender used under D1, and here it is set to the woman.
- [L3] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman." Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."
- [L2] The word behind "prepared" in Hebrews 10:5 is katartizo (G2675), to fit, to frame.
- [L4] The first promise puts the deliverer as the woman's seed. The body is prepared for him, and Luke 1:35 has it "born of thee." (Footed on L1 Genesis 3:15 + L2 zera' and katartizo + L3 Hebrews 10:5.)

**C4. Joseph is the husband, not the begetter, in the lineage.**

- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L2] Through Matthew 1:2-15 the verb is the active egennesen, "begat." In verse 16 it becomes the passive egennethe, "was born." The relative "of whom" is hes (the feminine singular of G3739), which can refer only to Mary. Joseph is called aner (G435), husband or man of Mary.
- [L3] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L4] The one place where the chain of begetting would reach Jesus changes its grammar to the woman's birth. The text gives Joseph the title of husband. (Footed on L1 Matthew 1:16 + L2 egennethe and hes.)

**C5. The defender's own D1 closes Joseph's loins.**

- [L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."
- [L1] Matthew 1:12: "after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel." Joseph's line (Matthew 1:16) runs down from Jechonias.
- [L1] Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- [L3] Luke 3:31 gives another line: "which was [the son] of Nathan, which was [the son] of David." 2 Samuel 7:12 requires seed "which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- [L4] A son of Joseph's loins is Jechonias's seed, and Jeremiah 22:30 bars Jechonias's seed from "sitting upon the throne of David." Yet the child receives that throne (Luke 1:32) and is David's seed "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). The flesh therefore comes from the woman's side, from David's line by Nathan. Joseph's seed would have forfeited the throne the angel gave. (Footed on L1 Jeremiah 22:30 + Matthew 1:12 + L1 Luke 1:32 + L3 Luke 3:31.)

## PRESSES AGAINST THE DEFENDER'S CHAIN

The defender's D2, D4 and D5 each rest on [L4] steps that lack the footing they claim. The witnesses below carry the answer.

**Premise 1. D5 is broken: the finding with child is "of the Holy Ghost" before the coming together.**

PRESSED WITH: Matthew 1:18; Matthew 1:20; Matthew 1:16.

- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] The defender reads synerchomai (G4905) as "cohabit" under one roof and puts the begetting inside the espousal, before the taking. But the narrator's word fixes the child's origin: ek pneumatos hagiou. This is the narrator's fact, set before any act of Joseph.
- [L3] Luke 2:5: "Mary his espoused wife, being great with child." At the birth journey she is still "espoused," after the taking of Matthew 1:24.
- [L4] The defender's "knew within the espousal" has no row that states a union. The only origin Matthew 1:18 gives for the child is the Holy Ghost. (Footed on L1 Matthew 1:18 + L2 ek and synerchomai + L3 Luke 2:5.)

**Premise 2. D5's reading of Matthew 1:19 fails.**

PRESSED WITH: Matthew 1:19; Matthew 1:20.

- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man]... was minded to put her away privily."
- [L2] The word is dikaios (G1342), just, equitable. Joseph "thought on these things" (Matthew 1:20). A just husband who knew himself the father of the child had no cause to put her away.
- [L1] The angel's "for" in Matthew 1:20 answers the thought: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The ground given for taking her is the Holy Ghost's origin of the child. It is not a covenant title.
- [L3] The defender's use of Mark 7:7-9 carries no row on Joseph. Mark 7:5 sets the scene: "Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?" That is the washing of hands. It is not Joseph's mind, and the inference "the child is Joseph's and he knew it" floats on one layer.

**Premise 3. D4's reading of Luke 1:35 fails.**

PRESSED WITH: Luke 1:34; Luke 1:35; Luke 1:37.

- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] Dio kai, "therefore also," stands inside verse 35, directly after the two clauses of the means. Those clauses are eperchomai (G1904, to come upon) and episkiazo (G1982, to overshadow). The title follows from the coming and overshadowing: "therefore."
- [L1] Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible." The question was how. The answer states a means, the Holy Ghost's coming, and ends on the impossible made possible. A husband's seed is not that.
- [L3] Luke 1:36 gives the sign of Elisabeth's old age. The comparison is between two impossibles, and an ordinary conception by a husband is not one.
- [L4] The defender's link of "therefore" back to Luke 1:32 passes over dio kai standing in verse 35's own clause. His reading stands on one layer where the same verse holds two. (Footed on L1 Luke 1:35 + L2 dio kai.)

**Premise 4. D2 and the sonship of Joseph are "supposed."**

PRESSED WITH: Luke 3:23; Luke 2:49; John 6:41-42.

- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L2] The word is nomizo (G3543), to deem. The defender cites Acts 16:13, where it is "wont," a custom.
- [L3] Acts 14:19 gives "supposing he had been dead," and Paul was not dead. Acts 21:29 gives "whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple," and he had not. In both the supposition is an opinion that does not match the fact.
- [L1] Luke 2:48 has Mary say "thy father and I." Luke 2:49 has the child answer: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The word "father" is turned to another Father.
- [L1] John 6:41-42: "The Jews then murmured at him... Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" The speakers are the murmurers, in reply to his claim to have come down from heaven.
- [L3] Mark 6:3: "the son of Mary." Reckoning by the mother stands in the record too.
- [L4] The "father" rows are speech of Mary (taking the legal place), of the narrator on the parents' legal standing, and of murmurers, set against a narrator who writes "as was supposed." (Footed on L1 Luke 3:23, 2:49 + L2 nomizo + L3 Acts 14:19 and 21:29.)

**Premise 5. D3 leaves room for a line through a woman.**

PRESSED WITH: Ezra 2:61; Numbers 1:2.

- [L1] Ezra 2:61: the priest "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name."
- [L4] The defender's own row has a man reckoned under the house of his wife's father. So "the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2) does not close Mary's side. (Footed on L1 Ezra 2:61 + L1 Numbers 1:2.)

**Premise 6. D4's "mingling" argument proves too much.**

PRESSED WITH: Leviticus 19:19; Hebrews 2:14; John 3:6.

- [L1] Genesis 2:7: "the LORD God formed man [of] the dust of the ground." This is flesh made by God with no father at all.
- [L1] Luke 3:38: "which was [the son] of Adam, which was [the son] of God." Sonship by God's making is stated of the first man.
- [L3] Romans 5:14: Adam "is the figure of him that was to come." 1 Corinthians 15:47: "the second man [is] the Lord from heaven."
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The flesh is the woman's, "of thee," as Hebrews 2:14 requires: "partakers of flesh and blood." The Holy Ghost sows no seed, so Leviticus 19:19, a statute for cattle and fields, has no mixed seed to forbid.
- [L4] The defender's own D4 says the Spirit did not beget flesh. The rule against mixing seed therefore has nothing to bar, and the flesh is of Mary, of her kind. (Footed on L1 Luke 1:35 + L1 Hebrews 2:14 + L3 Genesis 2:7, Luke 3:38.)

**Premise 7. D4's "Son of God" and Solomon fails.**

PRESSED WITH: 2 Samuel 7:14; 1 Chronicles 28:6; Romans 1:4.

- [L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him [to be] my son." Solomon's title is by choice, after birth.
- [L1] Luke 1:35: the title follows the conception: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- [L1] Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead. [declared: Gr. determined]"
- [L4] A declaration at the resurrection makes known a sonship the text already put at the conception. It does not move the origin. (Footed on L1 Luke 1:35 + Romans 1:4 + L3 1 Chronicles 28:6.)

**Charge:** The defender's inferences "Therefore Joseph is the named Davidic father" and "no begetting of flesh by the Spirit" lack the footing they claim. Premises 1 to 7 name the witnesses that break them.

I rest on this: Matthew 1:20 places the origin in the Holy Ghost, Isaiah 7:14 requires a virgin, Luke 1:35 gives the means, and Jeremiah 22:30 bars the seed of Joseph.

=== [DR2] ===
CHALLENGER (standard reading) -- ROUND 2, CLOSING AND PREMISE LIST

# CHALLENGER, ROUND 2 [DR2]

I take the reply premise by premise. Each answer below is graded against what the quoted verse carries.

## 1. Matthew 1:18: the finding comes before any coming together

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] "Before" is prin (G4250, prior, sooner). "Came together" is synerchomai (G4905, to cohabit conjugally). The child is found while the cohabiting is still prior, and the narrator gives its origin as pneuma hagion (G4151 and G40, Holy Ghost).

[L3] Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife." The "took" is paralambano (G3880, to receive near, to associate with oneself). The defender's own order, "the finding before the taking," puts the child in her before Joseph took her.

[L4] The defender takes "knew" in Matthew 1:25 back to a union inside the espousal. The rows give the opposite order. The child is found before the coming together, and its stated origin is the Holy Ghost. Genesis 4:1 and Ruth 4:13 are other couples, who "knew" and "went in." They cannot supply Joseph's act. [L4 footed on L1 Matthew 1:18, L2 prin and synerchomai, L3 Matthew 1:24.]

## 2. Matthew 1:16: the verb changes

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The defender calls this "non-narration" and says "It does not beget, it births." That grants the change of verb.

[L2] In Matthew 1:2 "begat" is the active gennao (G1080). In 1:16 the verb is passive, with the feminine relative "of whom." Joseph is called aner (G435, husband).

[L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac." Matthew 1:6: "David the king begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Urias."

[L4] The defender's reply is that "the rest of the witnesses fill what that one verse leaves quiet." This sets other verses over a verse that states the passive and the feminine. At the one place where the chain would reach Jesus, the grammar leaves the father's line and names the woman. [L4 footed on L1 Matthew 1:16, L2 gennao and aner, L3 Matthew 1:2 and 1:6.]

## 3. Matthew 1:19-20: the husband's mind and the angel's "for"

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man]... was minded to put her away privily." [L2] The word for "put away" is apolyo (G630, to dismiss, to divorce). It is joined to the "just" man of dikaios (G1342).

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "while he thought on these things." [L2] The word is enthymeomai (G1760, to ponder). The angel's answer is "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L4] The thinking concerns the woman's condition. The "for" meets it with the origin of the child, which is the Holy Ghost (Matthew 1:18). It does not meet it with a title. The Mark 7 rows the defender sets beside this are about washing: [L1] Mark 7:8, "the tradition of men, [as] the washing of pots and cups." [L3] Mark 7:5: "eat bread with unwashen hands." Joseph's decision is not in those verses, so "the child is his and he knew it" rests on them without footing. [L4 footed on L1 Matthew 1:19-20, L2 apolyo and enthymeomai, L3 Mark 7:5.]

## 4. Luke 1:34-37: the answer to "how"

[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L2] "How" is pos (G4459, in what way). The question is about means.

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] The two clauses are the means. Episkiazo (G1982) is "to invest with preternatural influence." The "therefore also" stands in the same sentence, after both clauses.

[L3] The defender's Acts 1:8, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you," is said to disciples already begotten. It is no answer to a question of how a virgin conceives.

[L1] Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible." [L2] The word is adynateo (G101, to be impossible). [L3] Luke 1:36 gives the barren's conceiving as the matching sign. The defender's reply names Zacharias in that chain. That is the husband's part, and it leaves the "how" of Luke 1:34-35 unanswered. [L4 footed on L1 Luke 1:35 and 1:37, L2 pos and episkiazo, L3 Luke 1:36.]

## 5. Luke 3:23 and Luke 2:48-49

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." [L2] The word is nomizo (G3543, to deem, to suppose). The defender says "Each context decides." So I read the context.

[L3] Acts 14:19, "supposing he had been dead," and Acts 21:29, "whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple," are both opinions set against the fact. Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made," attaches the custom-sense to a place, where "wont" is meaningful. Attached to "the son of Joseph" it would read "being wont the son." The sense that fits Luke 3:23 is the opinion that is set against the fact.

[L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L2] The word is pater (G3962, father). It answers Mary's "thy father" (Luke 2:48) with "my Father." The defender grants this as "the second Father." The child corrects the title. [L4 footed on L1 Luke 3:23 and 2:49, L2 nomizo and pater, L3 Acts 14:19 and 21:29.]

## 6. Jeremiah 22:30 and the throne

[L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."

[L1] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Joseph's line (Matthew 1:16) comes down through Jechonias. The defender grants that Jechonias had sons, and the verse is not about whether he had sons. It bars the seed from "sitting upon the throne of David."

[L3] Jeremiah 18:8 is spoken of a nation that turns from its evil, and Haggai 2:23 sets Zerubbabel as "my servant" and "signet."

[L1] Luke 1:32 gives the child "the throne of his father David." [L3] Luke 3:31 gives "Nathan, which was [the son] of David." [L2] Zera' (H2233, seed) in 2 Samuel 7:12 is satisfied by Nathan's line.

[L4] The defender's reply puts the bar aside through a conditional about a nation. The seed of Jechonias is barred from the throne, and the throne is given to the child. So the flesh of David's seed that Romans 1:3 names comes through the woman's line. [L4 footed on L1 Jeremiah 22:30 and Luke 1:32, L3 Luke 3:31 and Matthew 1:12.]

## 7. Isaiah 7:14: the KJV word is "virgin"

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." The defender writes "the young-woman word" for H5959 and says the sign is "bounded" in Isaiah's day. "Young woman" is not the KJV's word, and the KJV's word is the evidence here.

[L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child." [L3] Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]." Genesis 24:16 says of her: "a virgin, neither had any man known her." The defender's own list of H5959 also shows Song of Solomon 1:3 and 6:8, which the KJV renders "virgins."

[L1] Isaiah 7:11: "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above." [L4] A sign of that order cannot be a wife conceiving by her husband. The defender's Isaiah 8:3 has "the prophetess" who "conceived" after Isaiah "approached" her. That is a separate event, and it carries none of the words Isaiah 7:14 uses. [L4 footed on L1 Isaiah 7:11 and 7:14, L2 'almah and parthenos, L3 Genesis 24:16 and 24:43.]

UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES

1. LINK 5: The inference that a union of Joseph and Mary came within the espousal and begot the child props D5. The defender's words: "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins."
STEP: a union of husband and wife took place within the espousal and begot the child -- ASSUMES: a coming together of Joseph and Mary before the child was found in her -- ROWS GIVE: Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost"; Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"
PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" -- MEANS: the child is found in her before the coming together, with the Holy Ghost as its stated origin -- [L2] synerchomai (G4905, to cohabit conjugally) | [L3] Matthew 1:24 "took unto him his wife" | PROVEN IN [DR1]
Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" -- MEANS: the begetting named in the margin is placed in the Holy Ghost -- [L2] gennao (G1080, to procreate, properly of the father) | [L3] Matthew 1:18 "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" | PROVEN IN [DR1]
Luke 2:5 "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child." -- MEANS: after the taking she is still called espoused, so the defender's equation of coming together with taking does not reach the word "espoused" -- [L2] mnesteuo (G3423, to betroth) | [L3] Matthew 1:24 "took unto him his wife" | PROVEN IN [DR1]
Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" -- MEANS: the knowing the verse sets stands at the birth, after the finding with child -- [L2] ginosko (G1097, to know) | [L3] Genesis 4:1 "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain" | PROVEN IN [CR1]

2. LINK 5: The reading of Joseph's mind through the tradition of men props D5. The defender's words: "Joseph's unwillingness to make her a publick example IS his righteousness toward Mary his wife, against the scorn of men's tradition, and the child is his and he knew it."
STEP: Joseph's unwillingness to make her a public example is set against the tradition of men in Mark 7 -- ASSUMES: that the tradition of men in Mark 7:8 bears on Joseph's decision about Mary -- ROWS GIVE: Mark 7:8 "ye hold the tradition of men, [as] the washing of pots and cups"; Matthew 1:19 "was minded to put her away privily"
PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:19 "was minded to put her away privily" -- MEANS: a husband who knew himself the father would have no cause to be minded to put her away -- [L2] apolyo (G630, to dismiss, to divorce) | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" | PROVEN IN [DR1]
Matthew 1:20 "But while he thought on these things" -- MEANS: Joseph pondered a matter that the angel answers with the origin of the child, which is the Holy Ghost -- [L2] enthymeomai (G1760, to ponder) | [L3] Matthew 1:19 "was minded to put her away privily" | PROVEN IN [DR2]
Mark 7:8 "ye hold the tradition of men, [as] the washing of pots and cups" -- MEANS: the tradition in the verse is the washing of pots and cups, which is not Joseph's decision -- [L3] Mark 7:5 "Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?" | PROVEN IN [CR2]

3. LINK 4: The reading of Luke 1:35 as presence and anointing props D4. The defender's words: "Luke 1:35 is empowerment and presence, the Anointed named, not a begetting of flesh by the Spirit."
STEP: the Holy Ghost coming upon and overshadowing gives empowerment and presence, and the title -- ASSUMES: that Luke 1:35's answer to Mary's question is a power for witness, like the one given to the disciples -- ROWS GIVE: Luke 1:34 "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"; Luke 1:35 "that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God"
PRESSED WITH:
